extracted.intended_audience: researchers, university community, and readers interested in NIH funding equity and grant-allocation policy
extracted.subtask_description: Assessing models and criteria for allocating research grant funding (e.g., peer review, partial lottery, bibliometrics) with attention to fairness (racial disparities) and efficiency. The page summarizes a Correspondence arguing about how alternative models might perpetuate Black–white funding gaps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fairness of grant-allocation systems
rubrics_metrics.description: How can systems for allocating research grant funding be made more fair while improving their efficiency?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page highlights racial disparities as a central fairness concern; for example, in their study the overall award rate for Black applicants is 55% of that for white applicants. Evaluation should consider whether a model reduces such disparities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partial lottery as bias mitigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Funding proposals by partial lottery eliminates or at least alleviates bias — where winners are chosen randomly among applications that pass a round of peer review designed to cull the weakest proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether using a partial lottery after an initial review reduces evaluator bias versus traditional score-based selection, and whether it preserves sufficient quality/efficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of bibliometric measures (productivity and impact)
rubrics_metrics.description: Funding proposals on the basis of bibliometric measures such as productivity and impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess reliance on bibliometrics for selection, noting that such measures may reflect prior inequalities and could thus reproduce disparities rather than correct them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of peer review in culling weakest proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: A round of peer review designed to cull the weakest proposals is a step used in some alternative models (e.g., before a partial lottery).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate how effectively peer review distinguishes weak proposals from competitive ones and whether its processes introduce bias that carries forward into later selection stages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Susceptibility of allocation processes to perpetuate racial disparities
rubrics_metrics.description: These processes may unintentionally perpetuate racial disparities by reflecting inequalities from preliminary and/or previous decisions and criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When judging allocation models, examine whether selection criteria or upstream decisions (e.g., bibliometric-based measures, prior review outcomes) embed historical inequities that will maintain or exacerbate race-based funding gaps.
